josh (support): FYI customer Acme is seeing 500s when they exceed quota. They expect 429. Example response: `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: req-0a1b2c3d

{"error":"quota check failed"}`. Request ID above. Happening intermittently around 12:10 UTC.

megan (eng-sre): Oof. Can you paste the full request headers + the X-Request-ID and any backend logs you have? Also, what region?

josh (support): Sent logs to thread. Region us-west-2. Example curl we used to repro:```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Customer-ID: acme" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"spam"}'
``` Response body includes `quota backend timeout` in some cases. Correlation IDs: req-0a1b2c3d, req-0a1b2c9f.

rahul (eng-runtime): From traces I pulled for req-0a1b2c3d: the request was routed to `legacy-quota` pool due to an unintended route override from last night's rollout. legacy-quota started returning downstream timeouts (~1500ms) -> gateway transforms some dependency timeouts into 5xx. The quota service should return 429 for rate limit exceeded, but since the dependency timed out we saw 502/500.

megan (eng-sre): Can you share the gateway log snippet? need the exact upstream error mapping. Also has this affected other customers?

josh (support): Only Acme reported so far but logs show a small spike of similar errors for a handful of keys in us-west-2 at 12:08-12:14. Gateway log (sanitized):```
[12:09:21] req-0a1b2c3d route=edge-rategate -> upstream=legacy-quota error="upstream timeout" code=504
[12:09:21] req-0a1b2c3d gateway-response status=500 mapped_from=504 mapping_rule=fallthrough
```

rahul (eng-runtime): That mapping_rule `fallthrough` is the culprit. We have a bug where quota dependency timeouts (504) are being folded into an internal 500 instead of returning a 429/504 specialized handling. Also the route override caused traffic to hit legacy-quota which is slower under load. Repro steps: run short loop to hit quota then force legacy route:```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Customer-ID: acme" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"x"}' >/dev/null & done
``` After ~120 requests you'll see 500s instead of 429 if route points to legacy-quota.

megan (eng-sre): Temporary mitigation ideas? Can we flip routing back to the new quota service and patch the gateway mapping quickly?

rahul (eng-runtime): Yes. Plan: 1) Rollback route override to new-quota (config change) — low risk, should restore proper 429s. 2) Patch gateway mapping so that upstream quota timeouts return 504 or a 429-equivalent based on our classification instead of 500. 3) Add a short-circuit in the rategate that, if quota returns 5xx/timeout, responds with 429+retry-after for a known customer tier to avoid customer-visible 500s.

emily (customer-success): Acme is unhappy and asked for root cause + ETA. Can we give them a mitigation now and a fix ETA? They also asked whether any billing/overage counts were affected.

megan (eng-sre): ETA: rollback config in 10m (we tested staging), patch gateway mapping + canary in 60m, full rollout in 2h if canary looks good. For billing: if we returned 500 instead of 429, their requests likely retried and some could have been counted incorrectly — tagging billing. @finance-team please hold until we confirm classification.

josh (support): I told Acme we'll pause their retries and provide a postmortem. They disabled automated retry for now. Thanks.

deploy-bot: Initiating config rollback for route override (change id cfg-2026-03-17-rc2).

[12:20] deploy-bot: Rollback applied to us-west-2 edge-rategate routes.

megan (eng-sre): After rollback, verify customer: josh can you ask Acme to try the repro curl once more?

josh (support): Acme ran the same loop. They now see 429s consistently. Confirmed. :white_check_mark: 

rahul (eng-runtime): Good. Next: I'll open a PR to change gateway mapping + add the short-circuit logic. Will request an expedited review. PR diff will include mapping table change:```diff
- if upstream_error == "timeout": return 500
+ if upstream_error == "timeout": classify_quota_error(); // return 429 or 504 as appropriate
```

megan (eng-sre): Leaving thread open for the PR and postmortem. Thanks everyone. Paging summary to incident channel and will follow up with postmortem template.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by megan (eng-sre). Priority: P2.

josh (support): Added customer notes and next steps in the CRM ticket.

megan (eng-sre): Postmortem action items: 1) Fix mapping bug (rahul) 2) Add integration test for quota timeout classification (qa) 3) Improve routing rollout checks to avoid accidental legacy routing (infra) 4) Notify billing for investigation (finance).

emily (customer-success): I'll draft the customer-facing summary and share once PR is merged.

josh (support): Closing customer escalations after we confirm billing unchanged and PR merged.
